title: Chick-fil-A Community Scholars (2027-2028)
description: Thirteen $25,000 scholarships for community-service-minded leaders who plan to continue their education, based on academic success, community service and financial need. Recipients also join a year-long leadership development and mentoring program. Awards can be used for tuition, fees, books and education-related expenses at any accredited college, university or vocational/technical school.
unstructured_requirements: Must be planning to enroll (or already enrolled) in undergraduate or graduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the 2027-2028 academic year
Must be a resident of the United States, Puerto Rico or Canada
Must not be employed at a Chick-fil-A restaurant or Chick-fil-A, Inc. at the time of application, or be the dependent or spouse of a Chick-fil-A, Inc. employee or operator

gpa.quote: Have a minimum cumulative grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or the equivalent).

pay.quote: Every year, thirteen (13) $25,000 scholarships are awarded to students based on academic success, community service and financial need.

college.quote: accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school

title: Hagan Scholarship (2027-2028)
description: Nationwide need-based merit scholarship for students in the 2027 high school graduating class, providing $1,000 for essential items plus up to $7,500 per semester for up to 8 consecutive semesters at an eligible four-year college. Up to 1,500 scholarships can be awarded. Open regardless of citizenship.
unstructured_requirements: Parents' adjusted gross household income reported for 2025 federal income tax purposes must not have exceeded $125,000
Must enroll in an eligible four-year college or university the first fall semester after high school graduation (not a community college, junior college or online institution)
Must work 240 hours between January 1, 2027 and September 1, 2027 to be eligible for a fall semester disbursement
Must provide a high school transcript and an unsealed letter of recommendation
Must attend a high school located in the United States
compensation_description: $1,000 for essential items plus up to $7,500 each semester for up to 8 consecutive semesters

graduation.quote: For students in the 2027 high school graduating class.

gpa.quote: Must have achieved a 3.50 CGPA, be goal-driven, and willing to work to achieve their goals.

pay.quote: The scholarship provides $1,000 to help purchase essential items for college and up to $7,500 each semester for up to 8 consecutive semesters.

college.quote: Must enroll in an eligible four-year College or University the first fall semester following high school graduation.

title: Coolidge Scholarship (2026-27 cycle, for juniors)
description: Annually awarded, full-ride presidential scholarship covering tuition, room, board and expenses for four years of undergraduate study at any accredited U.S. college or university. High school juniors apply; finalists interview in Vermont with travel covered. Need-blind and open to any background and any field of study.
unstructured_requirements: Must intend to enroll full-time at an accredited U.S. college or university as an undergraduate for the first time in fall 2028 (no gap year)
Cannot be the immediate family member of a current employee, trustee or significant donor of the Calvin Coolidge Presidential Foundation or Fund
All application materials including letters of reference are due by the deadline
compensation_description: Full-ride: tuition, room, board and expenses for four years

grade.quote: students in their junior year of high school, or the equivalent if home schooled, are eligible to apply.

citizenship.quote: 2026-27 Coolidge Scholarship applicants must be citizens or legal permanent residents of the United States of America by the 2026-27 scholarship deadline.

pay.quote: The Coolidge Scholarship is an annually awarded, full-ride, presidential scholarship that covers a student’s tuition, room, board, and expenses for four years of undergraduate study.

college.quote: must intend to enroll full-time at an accredited U.S. college or university as an undergraduate

title: FRA Americanism Essay Contest 2026-2027 (grades 7-12)
description: Annual 350-word essay contest to promote the spirit of Americanism and patriotism, open to all students in grades 7 through 12 including home-schooled students. Entries go through an FRA member or local FRA branch, advance from local to regional to national judging, and national winners receive cash prizes. FRA branches are listed on the contest page, including in Maryland and Virginia.
unstructured_requirements: Essay must be 350 words and submitted through an FRA member or local FRA branch with the cover sheet
Use the 2026-2027 essay rules, cover sheet and poster from the contest page
compensation_description: Grand national winner $1,500; other national winners $1,000 (1st), $750 (2nd), $500 (3rd) in each category

grade.quote: FRA's Americanism Essay Contest is open to all students, grades 7 through 12, including those who are home schooled.

application_deadline.quote: Students are invited to submit a 350-word essay through an FRA member or local FRA branch before the December 1st deadline

dates.quote: Essay Poster 2026-2027 Essay Cover Sheet 2026-2027 Essay Rules 2026-2027

pay.quote: The grand national winner receives $1,500. Other winners receive $1,000 for first place, $750 for second place, and $500 for third place.

title: John F. Kennedy Profile in Courage Essay Contest 2027
description: National essay contest for U.S. high school students describing an act of political courage by a U.S. elected official who served during or after 1917 (700-1,000 words, at least five sources, with a nominating teacher). The winner receives $10,000; second place $3,000; three finalists $1,000 each.
unstructured_requirements: Essay must be 700 to 1,000 words with a minimum of five sources, and be the student's original work (essays are reviewed for AI assistance)
Must list a nominating teacher from your high school when submitting
Past winners and finalists, and employees of sponsors and their families, are not eligible
compensation_description: First place $10,000; second place $3,000; three finalists $1,000 each

grade.quote: United States high school students in grades nine through twelve attending public, private, parochial, or home schools

application_deadline.quote: The contest deadline is January 11, 2027 at 11:59 PM Eastern Standard Time.

pay.quote: The winner receives a $10,000 cash award.

title: Nancy Thorp Poetry Contest (63rd annual)
description: Poetry contest providing scholarships, prizes and recognition for the best poems by young women in their sophomore or junior year of high school. Submit one or two unpublished poems. Winners receive a cash prize, publication in Cargoes, and a renewable scholarship applicable if they enroll at Hollins.
unstructured_requirements: Open to young women in their sophomore or junior year of high school
Submit one or two poems of your best creative work; poems published previously or under consideration elsewhere are not eligible
compensation_description: Cash prize, publication, and a renewable scholarship of up to $5,000 per year (applicable if enrolled at Hollins)

grade.quote: the best poems submitted by young women in their sophomore or junior year of high school

citizenship.quote: Due to scholarship eligibility requirements, applicants must be a U.S. citizen

pay.quote: a renewable scholarship of up to $5,000 provided through the Creative Talent Award in Creative Writing for a total value of $20,000 in scholarship funds over four years (applicable if enrolled at Hollins)

title: Omega Psi Phi International High School Essay Contest 2026
description: Essay scholarship contest for college-bound high school seniors who submit an essay application through a local chapter of the fraternity. 2026 topic: "How can Young People use Leadership, Service, and Innovation to create Positive Change in their Communities?" (700-750 words). Scholarships of $2,000, $1,000 and $1,000.
unstructured_requirements: Must be college-bound and submit the essay application through a local chapter of the fraternity (reviewed by the chapter for your high school or home address)
Essay must be original, 700 to 750 words, typed and double-spaced, and use the exact essay topic

grade.quote: The Contest is open to all college-bound, high school seniors who submit an essay application through a Chapter of the Fraternity.

application_deadline.quote: Submissions will not be accepted after 11:59 PM, October 31, 2026.

title: Military Child of the Year Award 2027 (nominations)
description: Annual award recognizing outstanding military-connected young people ages 13 to 18, one for each branch of service, for scholarship, volunteerism, leadership and extracurricular involvement while facing the challenges of military family life. Recipients are flown with a parent or guardian to Washington, DC for the April 2027 gala and receive $10,000, a laptop and other gifts. A child is nominated by someone else.
unstructured_requirements: Child must be a legal military dependent (status confirmed by a DEERS enrollment form)
Nominee and one adult guardian must be available to travel to the Washington, DC area in April 2027 for the awards gala
compensation_description: $10,000, a laptop computer, and other donated gifts; travel to the Washington, DC gala

age.quote: Military children must be between the ages of 13 and 18, at the time of nomination.

pay.quote: They also will receive $10,000 each, a laptop computer, and other donated gifts.

application_deadline.quote: Submissions will close on December 1, 2026 at 11:59pm central.

title: VCU first-year university-level scholarships (Fall 2027, Nov. 1 deadline)
description: All incoming first-year students who apply to VCU by the first-year scholarship deadline are considered for university-level scholarships. VCU's regular decision deadline for first-years is Jan. 15, 2027.
unstructured_requirements: Apply for first-year admission to VCU by the scholarship deadline to be considered; no separate scholarship application is listed on this page

grade.quote: All incoming first-year students who apply to VCU by Nov. 1 are considered for university-level scholarships

title: Virginia Tech Stamps Scholarship (Early Action, Fall 2027)
description: Merit scholarship funding four years of estimated cost of attendance (tuition, fees, room and board) plus an enrichment fund for experiential learning. All students who apply to Virginia Tech by the Early Action deadline are considered based on their Virginia Tech and Common App materials; semi-finalists are contacted in mid-January and finalists interviewed in February.
unstructured_requirements: Must apply to Virginia Tech by the Early Action deadline; anyone applying after Early Action cannot be considered
Semi-finalists complete the Stamps Scholarship application on VT's Scholarship Central and interview with the Honors College faculty committee
compensation_description: Four years of funding for estimated cost of attendance (tuition, fees, room and board) plus an enrichment fund

grade.quote: All students applying to Virginia Tech Early Action (November 15 deadline) will be considered for the Stamps Scholarship.

application_deadline.quote: Applications for First-Year Early Action due November 15

dates.quote: Dates & Deadlines for 2026-2027 Applying for admissons to Virginia Tech

pay.quote: Virginia Tech Stamps Scholars receive funding for four years for estimated cost of attendance which includes tuition, fees, room, and board.

title: Toshiba/NSTA ExploraVision 2027
organization: Toshiba and the National Science Teaching Association (NSTA)
description: National STEM competition in which teams of students in grades K-12 (with a teacher or coach) envision how an existing technology could evolve in 10 or more years and submit a project description, abstract, bibliography and technology launch flyer. High School Level is grades 10-12; the oldest student on a team sets the category.
unstructured_requirements: Teams of students work with a teacher or coach, who submits the project online

Students must be U.S. or Canadian citizens living in the U.S., Canada, U.S. territories or a DoWEA school abroad, enrolled full-time in a public, private, parochial, virtual or home school, and no older than 21
High School Level is grades 10-12 (the oldest student on a team determines the category)

application_deadline.quote: The coach submits a team’s project online before the deadline of 8:00 PM ET, January 27, 2027.

title: Army ROTC Scholarship for the High School Class of 2027
description: Army ROTC scholarships for high school seniors, awarded based on academic achievement and usable at any of the 1,000+ participating schools, covering either tuition and fees or room and board. All ROTC scholarships also include a monthly allowance and an annual book stipend. Accepting means a future service obligation in the Army, Army Reserve or Army National Guard.
unstructured_requirements: Must be at least 17 and under 31 in the year of commissioning, and have a high school diploma or equivalent
Must have taken the SAT or ACT, pass the Army Physical Fitness Assessment, and meet the physical waist-to-height ratio standards
Accepting a scholarship means a future service obligation of eight years in the Army (active duty and/or Army Reserve or Army National Guard, depending on the scholarship)
Board rounds: Round 01 due Oct. 12, 2026, Round 02 due Jan. 18, 2027, Round 03 due Mar. 8, 2027; applications must be started no later than Mar. 4, 2027
compensation_description: Tuition and fees or room and board, plus $420 per month and $1,200 per year for books

grade.quote: for the High School Class of 2027 for the 2026 – 2027 school year.

citizenship.quote: Be a U.S. citizen Be at least 17 and under 31 in year of commissioning

gpa.quote: Have an unweighted high school GPA of at least 2.50 if you’re in high school while applying

pay.quote: All ROTC scholarships include an extra $420 each month throughout the school year for expenses like housing, along with $1,200 each year to spend on books.

application_open_date.quote: ROTC scholarship applications open on June 14, 2026.

application_deadline.quote: Applications must be started no later than March 4, 2027 to be eligible for review by the Army ROTC National Scholarship Board

title: Air Force ROTC High School Scholarship Program (2027-2028 academic year)
description: Air Force ROTC scholarships for students who will enter college and the AFROTC program in the 2027-2028 academic year. Capped and uncapped tuition scholarship types are available, an annual book stipend of $900 and a monthly stipend, and a recipient can convert benefits to a room scholarship. Accepting a scholarship creates a service obligation as an officer in the Air Force or Space Force.
unstructured_requirements: Must be a U.S. citizen, or obtain U.S. citizenship by the last day of the first term of the freshman year
Must have an SAT composite of 1310, ACT composite of 28 or CLT composite of 93 (no super scores; the ACT Science portion must be taken)
Must complete the Physical Fitness Assessment (push-ups, crunches and a 2.0 mile run) and, if awarded, pass a DoDMERB medical exam
If awarded, you must accept a commission as an Air Force or Space Force officer and serve at least four years on active duty; if you are under legal age, a parent or guardian must sign the agreement
compensation_description: Tuition scholarship (capped or uncapped), $900 annual book stipend, and a monthly stipend of $300 (freshman) to $500 (senior)

grade.quote: Completion of your junior year of high school is required for all ROTC applications.

gpa.quote: Cumulative unweighted GPA of 3.3 or higher.

application_open_date.quote: The scholarship application window will be open July 1, 2026, through December 11, 2026.

application_deadline.quote: The scholarship application window will be open July 1, 2026, through December 11, 2026.

pay.quote: The annual book stipend is $900 per academic year, and the monthly stipend increases based on an individual’s student status. Freshman: $300 Sophomore: $350 Junior: $450 Senior: $500
